subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw doctor --fix 4-5x slower on 2026.5.20 vs 2026.5.19 (55s → 229s+) — session snapshot path traversal bottleneck

question: Should maintainers continue tracking the remaining doctor/update slowdown through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85670, replace it with a narrower measured fix, or close only after live timing proof shows current releases are fast enough?
rationale: Current code and the latest release ship the stale snapshot repair but not the remaining repair-sequencing optimization, and the open candidate is blocked by proof plus auth-ordering risk that automation should not resolve by duplicating work.

options.title: Keep Open For Proven Narrow Fix
options.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical umbrella while the A1 branch is repaired or replaced with a narrower optimization that preserves auth ordering and includes redacted before/after timing proof.

options.title: Close After Live Release Proof
options.body: Close only if a maintainer obtains comparable current-release timing showing the reported multi-session update/doctor path no longer regresses.

options.title: Accept Remaining Slow Path
options.body: Explicitly decide that the shipped snapshot repair is enough and document that deeper doctor performance work is not planned right now.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Proven Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical umbrella while the A1 branch is repaired or replaced with a narrower optimization that preserves auth ordering and includes redacted before/after timing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the shipped snapshot repair and is the strongest routing candidate for deciding whether the remaining blocked optimization should be repaired, replaced, or closed with proof.
